quick: HTN: 2.5 mg once daily, titrate to 2.5-20 mg/day
With or without food; may open capsule onto applesauce
Contraindicated; boxed warning for fetal toxicity (discontinue ASAP)
If CrCl <40 mL/min, start 1.25 mg/day; reduce dose
Use caution; reduced conversion, elevated ramipril levels
summary: Ramipril is a long-acting ACE inhibitor (a prodrug converted to active ramiprilat) used to treat hypertension and to improve survival in stable patients with clinical heart failure following acute myocardial infarction. It lowers blood pressure by suppressing the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system, reducing angiotensin II and aldosterone. Carries a boxed warning for fetal toxicity and must be discontinued when pregnancy is detected. Class effects include cough, hyperkalemia, angioedema, and renal function changes requiring monitoring.
indications: Stable patients with clinical signs of congestive heart failure within the first few days after acute myocardial infarction (reduces risk of death, heart failure hospitalization, and progression to severe heart failure)

dosage.d: Initial 2.5 mg once daily (patients not on a diuretic); usual maintenance 2.5-20 mg/day
dosage.t: Adjust per BP response after 2-4 weeks; may give as single dose or two divided doses
dosage.n: If effect wanes toward end of interval, consider higher dose or twice-daily dosing; add diuretic if BP uncontrolled

dosage.d: Start 2.5 mg twice daily (5 mg/day); target 5 mg twice daily
dosage.t: After 1 week, increase as tolerated toward target with increases about 3 weeks apart
dosage.n: If hypotensive at 2.5 mg BID, reduce to 1.25 mg twice daily; observe under supervision for at least 2 h after first dose and until BP stable for an additional hour

dosage.d: Initial 1.25 mg once daily; max total 5 mg/day
dosage.n: Establish baseline renal function before initiating

dosage.c: Heart failure post-MI with renal impairment
dosage.d: Initial 1.25 mg once daily; may increase to 1.25 mg twice daily, up to max 2.5 mg twice daily

dosage.c: Volume depletion or renal artery stenosis

admin: Swallow capsules whole, or open and sprinkle contents onto about 4 oz (120 mL) of applesauce, water, or apple juice
If mixed, consume the entire mixture to ensure full dose; prepared mixtures may be stored up to 24 h at room temperature or 48 h refrigerated
May be taken with or without food (food slows but does not significantly reduce absorption)
Correct volume and salt depletion before starting therapy to reduce risk of hypotension
Avoid potassium supplements, potassium-containing salt substitutes, and potassium-sparing diuretics unless directed
moa: Ramipril is hydrolyzed (primarily by hepatic esterases) to its active diacid metabolite ramiprilat, which inhibits angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE, kininase II). This blocks conversion of angiotensin I to the vasoconstrictor angiotensin II, lowering vasopressor activity and aldosterone secretion (with a small rise in serum potassium) and increasing plasma renin activity. ACE inhibition also reduces degradation of bradykinin, which may contribute to vasodilation and to the characteristic cough.

absolute: History of angioedema related to prior ACE inhibitor therapy
History of hereditary or idiopathic angioedema
Hypersensitivity to ramipril or any other ACE inhibitor
relative: Concomitant aliskiren in patients with diabetes or renal impairment (dual RAAS blockade)
Concomitant telmisartan or other ARB/RAAS blocker (not recommended)
Severe congestive heart failure (risk of azotemia/acute renal failure)
Collagen-vascular disease with renal impairment (hematologic risk)
monitor: Renal function (BUN/creatinine), especially first weeks and with diuretic or NSAID use
White blood cell counts in collagen-vascular disease
Hepatic enzymes/bilirubin if signs of cholestasis or jaundice

preg: Boxed warning - fetal toxicity. Drugs acting on the renin-angiotensin system used in the second and third trimesters reduce fetal renal function and increase fetal/neonatal morbidity and death; oligohydramnios may cause fetal lung hypoplasia and skeletal deformations, and neonatal skull hypoplasia, anuria, hypotension, and renal failure may occur. (Former Pregnancy Category D.) Discontinue ramipril as soon as pregnancy is detected. If no alternative exists, counsel on fetal risk and perform serial ultrasounds; discontinue if oligohydramnios occurs unless lifesaving for the mother.
lact: Not recommended in nursing mothers. A single 10 mg oral dose produced undetectable amounts of ramipril and metabolites in breast milk, but multiple doses may produce low, unpredictable milk concentrations.
renal: Establish baseline renal function before starting. For CrCl >40 mL/min, usual regimens may be followed. For more severe impairment, about 25% of the usual dose produces full therapeutic ramiprilat levels. Hypertension with renal impairment: start 1.25 mg once daily, titrate to max 5 mg/day. Heart failure post-MI with renal impairment: start 1.25 mg once daily, up to max 2.5 mg twice daily. With CrCl <40 mL/min/1.73 m2, peak ramiprilat levels roughly double and AUC is 3-4 times higher; monitor renal function and potassium closely.
hepatic: Ramipril is metabolized by hepatic esterases to active ramiprilat; in hepatic impairment this conversion is slowed and plasma ramipril levels rise about 3-fold (peak ramiprilat levels and effect on ACE activity are not notably different). No formal dosing studies in hypertensive patients with hepatic impairment; use with caution. Discontinue if jaundice or marked hepatic enzyme elevations occur (rare risk of cholestatic jaundice progressing to fulminant hepatic necrosis).

major: Aliskiren (avoid in diabetes/renal impairment - dual RAAS blockade increases hyperkalemia, hypotension, renal dysfunction)
Telmisartan/other ARBs (combination not recommended - increased renal dysfunction per ONTARGET)
Potassium-sparing diuretics (spironolactone, amiloride, triamterene), potassium supplements, potassium-containing salt substitutes (hyperkalemia)
moderate: Diuretics (excessive hypotension, especially if recently started)
Lithium (increased lithium levels and toxicity - monitor levels)
NSAIDs including selective COX-2 inhibitors (reduced antihypertensive effect; risk of renal deterioration/acute renal failure in elderly, volume-depleted, or renally impaired)
minor: No clinically significant interaction reported with digoxin, antacids, furosemide, cimetidine, indomethacin, simvastatin, warfarin, or phenprocoumon
interactions.food: Not significantly affected by food; rate of absorption is reduced but extent and ramiprilat levels are unaffected.
interactions.alcohol: Alcohol may potentiate the blood-pressure-lowering effect and worsen hypotension/dizziness; advise caution.
interactions.diagnostics: May increase serum potassium, BUN, and creatinine; elevations of liver enzymes, bilirubin, uric acid, and blood glucose, plus hyponatremia, have been reported. Anaphylactoid reactions reported with high-flux dialysis membranes and LDL apheresis with dextran sulfate.

rare: Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis, pemphigus
emergency: Angioedema of face, lips, tongue, glottis, or larynx (can be fatal - may need subcutaneous epinephrine and airway management)
Intestinal angioedema (abdominal pain with/without nausea or vomiting)

monitoring: Blood pressure (and observe at least 2 h after first dose in post-MI heart failure)
Renal function (BUN, serum creatinine), especially first weeks and with diuretic/NSAID use
White blood cell counts in patients with collagen-vascular disease and renal impairment
Hepatic enzymes and bilirubin if signs of hepatic dysfunction
counsel: Report immediately any swelling of the face, eyes, lips, or tongue or any difficulty breathing, and stop the drug until you contact your prescriber (angioedema)
Report any sign of infection such as sore throat or fever (possible neutropenia)
Light-headedness can occur, especially in the first days; report it, and stop the drug and follow up if fainting occurs
Inadequate fluid intake, excessive sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting can cause an excessive fall in blood pressure
Do not use potassium-containing salt substitutes without consulting your physician
Women of childbearing age should know the risks in pregnancy; report a suspected pregnancy as soon as possible
A dry, persistent cough may occur and resolves after stopping the drug
pk: BP lowering within 1-2 h of a single dose
Ramipril Cmax within 1 h; ramiprilat 2-4 h; peak BP effect 3-6 h
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); light-resistant, tight container
pearls: Prodrug: ramipril is converted by hepatic esterases to active ramiprilat, which has about 6 times the ACE-inhibitory activity
ACE-inhibitor cough is bradykinin-mediated, nonproductive, and resolves after discontinuation; switching to an ARB is a common alternative
ACE inhibitors cause higher rates of angioedema in Black patients; class also less effective as monotherapy in low-renin Black hypertensives
Avoid dual RAAS blockade (with ARBs or aliskiren) - no added benefit and increased renal dysfunction/hyperkalemia (ONTARGET)
In post-MI heart failure (AIRE trial), ramipril reduced all-cause mortality by 27%
Hold or reduce concomitant diuretic and correct volume depletion before initiation to limit first-dose hypotension
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the regular schedule. Do not take two doses at once to make up for a missed dose.
overdose: Most likely manifestation is symptomatic hypotension. Treat by infusion of normal (physiological) saline to expand volume; place the patient supine. Serum drug-level measurements have no established role, and no maneuvers are established to accelerate elimination; it is not known whether ramipril/ramiprilat are effectively removed by hemodialysis. Angiotensin II could theoretically serve as a specific antidote but is essentially unavailable. Provide supportive care.
